Poem: 市中は　物のにほひや　夏の月
Romaji: ichinaka wa / mono no nioi ya / natsu no tsuki
My translation:
in the city —
the fragrance of things . . .
summer moon
Kigo: 夏の月 natsu no tsuki (summer moon)
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: あつしあつしと　門々の声
Romaji: atsushi atsushi to / kadokado no koe
My translation:
so hot, so hot —
voices at every gate
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 二番草　取りも果たさず　穂に出でて
Romaji: nibangusa / tori mo hatasazu / ho ni idete
My translation:
the second weeding
not yet finished —
ears of grain appear
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 灰うちたたく　宵の稲妻
Romaji: hai uchitaku / yoi no inazuma
My translation:
ashes beaten and scattered —
lightning at dusk
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 此の筋は　銀も見しらず　不自由さよ
Romaji: kono suji wa / gin mo mishirazu / fujiyū sa yo
My translation:
in this trade
silver goes unrecognized —
what inconvenience
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: ただとひやうしに　長き脇指
Romaji: tada to hyōshi ni / nagaki wakizashi
My translation:
drawn by chance alone —
a long short sword
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 北野どの　御すきもの　梅の花
Romaji: Kitano-dono / o-suki mono / ume no hana
My translation:
lord of Kitano —
what he loves best:
the plum blossom
Kigo: 梅の花 ume no hana (plum blossoms)
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: かめにさす　柳のさけや　つくりばな
Romaji: kame ni sasu / yanagi no sake ya / tsukuribana
My translation:
steeped in the jar —
willow-branch sake,
artificial flowers
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 風さむし　やぶれ障子の　神無月
Romaji: kaze samushi / yabureshōji no / kannazuki
My translation:
the wind is cold —
through a torn shoji,
the godless month
Kigo: 神無月 kannazuki (tenth month; the godless month)
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: きえくとも　火にならりそ　雪ぼとけ
Romaji: kieku tomo / hi ni narariso / yukibotoke
My translation:
though you melt away —
do not get used to fire,
snow buddha
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 寒くとも　これまことの　雪ほとけ
Romaji: samuku tomo / kore makoto no / yukibotoke
My translation:
though it is cold —
this is the true one,
snow buddha
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: にがにがしい　つままで嵐　ふきの蕾
Romaji: niganigashii / tsuma made arashi / fuki no tsubomi
My translation:
how disagreeable —
a storm even to pluck
the coltsfoot buds
Kigo: ふきの蕾 fuki no tsubomi (coltsfoot buds)
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 春さむし　いつまで嵐　ふきの薹
Romaji: haru samushi / itsu made arashi / fuki no tō
My translation:
spring is cold —
how long will the storm blow,
coltsfoot shoots
Kigo: ふきの薹 fuki no tō (coltsfoot shoots)
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 飛梅　やからろがろしくも　神の春
Romaji: tobiumé ya / kakarogaroshi ku mo / kami no haru
My translation:
the flying plum —
how lightly it moves,
spring of the god
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 青柳の　まゆかく　岸のひたひかな
Romaji: aoyagi no / mayukaku / kishi no hitahi kana
My translation:
the green willow
draws its brows —
the forehead of the bank
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 花よりも　鼻にありけるに　ほひかな
Romaji: hana yori mo / hana ni arikeru / nioi kana
My translation:
more than the blossoms —
it was in the nose all along,
that fragrance
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: かさきぎや　今日久かたの　雨の川
Romaji: kasakigi ya / kyō hisakata no / ame no kawa
My translation:
umbrella trees —
today, after all this time,
rain on the river
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 霞きへ　まだらにありて　たらの年
Romaji: kasumi kie / madara ni arite / tara no toshi
My translation:
the mist dissolves —
dappled and lingering,
another year
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 山の腰に　ひるねの種や　秋の月
Romaji: yama no koshi ni / hirune no tane ya / aki no tsuki
My translation:
at the mountain's waist —
seeds of an afternoon nap,
autumn moon
Kigo: 秋の月 aki no tsuki (autumn moon)
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 花よりも　団子にありて　帰る雁
Romaji: hana yori mo / dango ni arite / kaeru kari
My translation:
more than the blossoms —
it's the dumplings that matter,
geese returning
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 皆人の　夕だちや　雲の帯
Romaji: mina hito no / yūdachi ya / kumo no obi
My translation:
everyone caught —
in the evening shower,
a sash of cloud
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 秋やら今朝　一足に知るの　ごひ縁
Romaji: aki yara kesa / hitoashi ni shiru no / goi-en
My translation:
is it autumn already —
in a single step, knowing:
the sound of a rake
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: やあしばらく　花に酔へる　雲の乱れ足
Romaji: yā shibaraku / hana ni yoeru / kumo no midarashi
My translation:
wait — just a moment —
drunk on blossoms,
the cloud's staggering step
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 天も花に　酔へる　鐘撞く事
Romaji: ten mo hana ni / yoeru / kane tsuku koto
My translation:
even heaven drunk on blossoms —
the tolling of the bell
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: かをり来て　目に酔ひたまる　梅の花
Romaji: kaori kite / me ni yoi tamaru / ume no hana
My translation:
the fragrance drifts in —
pooling behind the eyes,
plum blossoms
Kigo: 梅の花 ume no hana (plum blossoms)
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: これはこれはとばかり花の吉野山
Romaji: kore wa kore wa to / bakari / hana no Yoshinoyama
My translation:
oh — oh —"
there are no other words:
the blossoms of Yoshino
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 歌いくさ　文武二道の　蛙かな
Romaji: utaikusa / bunbu futamichi no / kawazu kana
My translation:
the singing contest —
frogs versed in both
the ways of pen and sword
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 福の神を　今日乗せ来るや　午の年
Romaji: fuku no kami wo / kyō nose kuru ya / uma no toshi
My translation:
carrying the god of fortune —
arriving today:
the year of the horse
Kigo: 午の年 uma no toshi (year of the horse)
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 若竹の心かけ樋や　軒のつま
Romaji: wakatake no / kokoro kake-toi ya / noki no tsuma
My translation:
the young bamboo's heart —
a hanging gutter,
the eaves' edge
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 一僕とほくほくありく　花見かな
Romaji: hitori boku / tōku tōku ariku / hanami kana
My translation:
one servant boy
walking on and on —
flower-viewing
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 春立つや　人の心を　うご霞
Romaji: haru tatsu ya / hito no kokoro wo / ugo kasumi
My translation:
spring arrives —
stirring the hearts of people,
the haze
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 春立つや　にほんめで　たき門の松
Romaji: haru tatsu ya / Nihon mede / taki kado no matsu
My translation:
spring arrives —
a Japan worth celebrating:
the pine at the gate
Notes: Chapter 1: From Muromachi Haikai to Teimon Haikai

Poem: 里人の　わたり候　頚の霜
Romaji: sato hito no / watari sōrō / kubi no shimo
My translation:
the village folk —
do you pass this way?"
frost on the neck
Notes: Chapter 2: The Novelty of Danrin Haikai

Poem: ながむとて　花にもいたく　慣れぬれば
Romaji: nagamu tote / hana ni mo itaku / narenareba
My translation:
gazing so long —
even the blossoms start to hurt,
grown too familiar
Notes: Chapter 2: The Novelty of Danrin Haikai

Poem: 今こんと　いひひしばも　かたし　頚の料理の骨
Romaji: ima kon to / iihishiba mo / katashi kubi no ryōri no hone
My translation:
i'll come right now, you said —
and now it's all that's hard:
bones of a neck dish
Notes: Chapter 2: The Novelty of Danrin Haikai

Poem: 鶯を　日毎に　きけと　興は有りて
Romaji: uguisu wo / higoto ni kike to / kyō wa arite
My translation:
listen to the warbler —
every day, they say,
and today there is delight
俳人: 西鶴, as Tsuruyuki 鶴永
Notes: Chapter 2: The Novelty of Danrin Haikai

Poem: 飛梅　ふるきも　又あらたなると　神の春
Romaji: tobiumé / furuki mo mata / arata naru to / kami no haru
My translation:
the flying plum —
the old becomes new again,
spring of the god
Notes: Chapter 2: The Novelty of Danrin Haikai

Poem: 山　ふかく　入る　旅　ぎせる　霧　こめて
Romaji: yama fukaku / iru tabi / giseru / kiri komete
My translation:
deep into the mountain —
a traveller's pipe,
wrapped in mist
Notes: Chapter 2: The Novelty of Danrin Haikai

Poem: 革巾　着　やいつの　珊瑚　小　鹿
Romaji: kawakignu / ki ya itsu no / sango ko-jika
My translation:
a leather purse —
when was the little deer
turned to coral?
Notes: Chapter 2: The Novelty of Danrin Haikai

Poem: 天川に　紅葉　ながる　珊珠　男
Romaji: Amakawa ni / momiji nagaru / sanju otoko
My translation:
on the Amakawa —
autumn leaves drifting,
a coral man
Notes: Chapter 2: The Novelty of Danrin Haikai

Poem: 咲く花や　懐紙合はせて　四百本
Romaji: saku hana ya / kaishi awasete / yonhyaku-hon
My translation:
blossoms in bloom —
four hundred sheets of paper
bound together
Notes: Chapter 2: The Novelty of Danrin Haikai

Poem: 水引　壱　把　青柳の　糸
Romaji: mizuhiki / ichi wa / aoyagi no ito
My translation:
one bundle of cord —
threads of the green willow
Notes: Chapter 2: The Novelty of Danrin Haikai

Poem: 春風を　おさむる　へぎに　熨斗添へて
Romaji: harukaze wo / osamuru / hegi ni / noshi soete
My translation:
the spring wind contained —
in a thin cedar box,
with a gift-strip attached
Notes: Chapter 2: The Novelty of Danrin Haikai

Poem: しれぬ世や　釈迦の死に跡に　金がある
Romaji: shirenu yo ya / Shaka no shiniatoni / kane ga aru
My translation:
this world makes no sense —
where the Buddha died,
there is money
Notes: Chapter 2: The Novelty of Danrin Haikai

Poem: 大晦日　定めなき世の　さだめかな
Romaji: ōmisoka / sadame naki yo no / sadame kana
My translation:
new year's eve —
the one fixed point
in a world without fixity
Notes: Chapter 2: The Novelty of Danrin Haikai

Poem: 今朝国土　笑はせ初めぬ　俳諧師
Romaji: kesa kokudo / warawase somenu / haikaishi
My translation:
this morning the whole land —
made to laugh for the first time:
a haikai master
Notes: Chapter 2: The Novelty of Danrin Haikai

Poem: 木之の端の　法師肥えや　花の暮
Romaji: kinohate no / hōshi koe ya / hana no kure
My translation:
at the edge of the grove —
a fat priest,
evening blossoms
Notes: Chapter 2: The Novelty of Danrin Haikai

Poem: 蛇之助が　恨みの鐘や　桜の雪
Romaji: Janoske ga / urami no kane ya / sakura no yuki
My translation:
Janoske's bell of resentment —
cherry-blossom snow
Notes: Chapter 2: The Novelty of Danrin Haikai

Poem: 恥ぞつむ　我が　窓の　網引かな
Romaji: haji zo tsumu / waga / mado no / ami-hiki kana
My translation:
shame piles up —
at my window,
hauling the nets
Notes: Chapter 2: The Novelty of Danrin Haikai

Poem: 見えにけり　くつその　かみ　八岐の大生海鼠へ
Romaji: mie ni keri / kutsuso no kami / Yamata no ōnamako e
My translation:
now it appears —
the god of shoes,
toward the great eight-branched sea-slug
Notes: Chapter 2: The Novelty of Danrin Haikai

Poem: 酢瓶に　けり蚤の　都のおもてふが
Romaji: su-kame ni / keri nomi no / miyako no omote fuga
My translation:
into the vinegar jar —
a flea's elegant capital,
its surface refined
Notes: Chapter 2: The Novelty of Danrin Haikai

Poem: 富士に傍うて　三月七日八日かな
Romaji: Fuji ni sobaute / sangatsu nanuka yōka kana
My translation:
keeping close to Fuji —
the seventh and eighth
of the third month
Notes: Chapter 3: The Sprouting of a New Wind

Poem: 稲妻に　片日影　ゆく棺
Romaji: inazuma ni / katahikage / yuku hitsugi
My translation:
in a flash of lightning —
half in shadow,
a passing coffin
Notes: Chapter 3: The Sprouting of a New Wind

Poem: 月一つ　柳ち残る　木の間より
Romaji: tsuki hitotsu / yanagi chinokoru / koma yori
My translation:
one moon —
a willow still remaining,
through the trees
Notes: Chapter 3: The Sprouting of a New Wind

Poem: 綿の花　たまたま蘭に　似たるかな
Romaji: wata no hana / tamatama ran ni / nitaru kana
My translation:
the cotton flower —
by chance resembling
an orchid
Kigo: 綿の花 wata no hana (cotton flower)
Notes: Chapter 3: The Sprouting of a New Wind

Poem: しら雲を　吹き尽くしたる　新樹かな
Romaji: shirakumo wo / fukitsukushitaru / shinjukana
My translation:
having blown away
every last white cloud —
fresh young leaves
Notes: Chapter 3: The Sprouting of a New Wind

Poem: 笹の葉に　西日のめぐる　時雨かな
Romaji: sasa no ha ni / nishi-hi no meguru / shigure kana
My translation:
on the bamboo leaves —
the western sun turning
through the winter drizzle
Notes: Chapter 3: The Sprouting of a New Wind

Poem: 芋洗ふ　女に月は　落ちにけり
Romaji: imo arau / onna ni tsuki wa / ochi ni keri
My translation:
washing the taro —
onto the woman
the moon has fallen
Notes: Chapter 3: The Sprouting of a New Wind

Poem: 夜や秋や　海士のやせ子や　鳴く鷗
Romaji: yo ya aki ya / ama no yaseko ya / naku kamome
My translation:
is it night, is it autumn —
is she a diver's thin child?
the crying gull
Notes: Chapter 3: The Sprouting of a New Wind

Poem: 菜の花や　淀も桂も　すれわれ夕涼み
Romaji: na no hana ya / Yodo mo Katsura mo / sure-ware yūsuzumi
My translation:
rapeseed blossoms —
the Yodo and the Katsura too
rubbing past us in the evening cool
Kigo: 菜の花 na no hana (rapeseed blossoms)
Notes: Chapter 3: The Sprouting of a New Wind

Poem: 春の夢　気の違はぬ　うらめしい
Romaji: haru no yume / ki no tagawanu / urameshii
My translation:
a spring dream —
how resentful
that I didn't lose my mind
Kigo: 春の夢 haru no yume (spring dream)
Notes: Chapter 3: The Sprouting of a New Wind

Poem: 行水も　日まぜになりぬ　虫のこゑ
Romaji: gyōzui mo / himazeni narinu / mushi no koe
My translation:
the outdoor bath
now taken every other day —
voices of insects
Kigo: 虫の声 mushi no koe (insect voices)
Notes: Chapter 3: The Sprouting of a New Wind

Poem: 元日や　されば野川の　水の音
Romaji: ganjitsu ya / sareba nogawa no / mizu no oto
My translation:
new year's day —
and so, the sound of water
in the field stream
Notes: Chapter 3: The Sprouting of a New Wind

Poem: 白魚や　きながらうこく　水の色
Romaji: shirauo ya / kinagara ugoku / mizu no iro
My translation:
whitebait —
moving while still alive,
the colour of water
Notes: Chapter 3: The Sprouting of a New Wind

Poem: 水ふんで草で足ふく　夏野かな
Romaji: mizu funde / kusa de ashi fuku / natsuno kana
My translation:
stepping through water —
wiping one's feet on grass:
a summer field
Notes: Chapter 3: The Sprouting of a New Wind

Poem: 行水も　日まぜになりぬ　虫のこゑ
Romaji: gyōzui mo / himazeni narinu / mushi no koe
My translation:
the outdoor bath
now every other day —
insect voices
Kigo: 虫の声 mushi no koe (insect voices)
Notes: Chapter 3: The Sprouting of a New Wind

Poem: 雪の朝　独り干鮭を　噛み得タリ
Romaji: yuki no asa / hitori karazake wo / kami etari
My translation:
a snowy morning —
alone, I manage
to gnaw dried salmon
Notes: Chapter 3: The Sprouting of a New Wind

Poem: いづる鶯　声波ヲうって　腸氷ル夜やなみだ
Romaji: izuru uguisu / koe nami wo utte / harawata koōru yoru ya namida
My translation:
the warbler emerges —
its cry strikes the waves,
a night of frozen entrails and tears
Notes: Chapter 3: The Sprouting of a New Wind

Poem: 芭蕉野分して　望に雨を聞く夜かな
Romaji: bashō nowaki shite / nozomi ni ame wo kiku yoru kana
My translation:
the banana plant torn by storm —
a night of listening
to rain in a basin
Notes: Chapter 3: The Sprouting of a New Wind

Poem: 野ざらしを　心に風の　しむ身かな
Romaji: nozarashi wo / kokoro ni kaze no / shimu mi kana
My translation:
resolved to be
a bleached skeleton —
the wind cuts to the bone
Notes: Chapter 3: The Sprouting of a New Wind

Poem: 猿を聞く人　捨て子に秋の風いかに
Romaji: saru wo kiku hito / sutego ni aki no / kaze ikani
My translation:
you who hear the monkey cry —
what of the abandoned child
in the autumn wind?
Kigo: 秋の風 aki no kaze (autumn wind)
Notes: Chapter 3: The Sprouting of a New Wind

Poem: 山路来て　何やらゆかし　すみれ草
Romaji: yamaji kite / naniyara yukashi / sumire gusa
My translation:
coming along a mountain path —
something strangely moving:
violets
Notes: Chapter 3: The Sprouting of a New Wind

Poem: 古池や　蛙飛びこむ　水の音
Romaji: furuike ya / kawazu tobikomu / mizu no oto
My translation:
the ancient pond —
a frog leaps in,
sound of water
Notes: Chapter 4: The World of Bashō

Poem: 鷹一つ　見付けてうれしい　いらこ崎
Romaji: taka hitotsu / mitsukete ureshi / Irako-zaki
My translation:
one hawk found —
what joy:
Cape Irako
Notes: Chapter 4: The World of Bashō

Poem: おもしろうて　やがて悲しき　鵜舟かな
Romaji: omoshiroute / yagate kanashiki / ubune kana
My translation:
delightful —
and soon after, sad:
the cormorant boats
Notes: Chapter 4: The World of Bashō

Poem: 吹きとばす　石はあさまの　野分かな
Romaji: fukitobasu / ishi wa Asama no / nowaki kana
My translation:
blowing away the stones —
Mt. Asama's
autumn gale
Notes: Chapter 4: The World of Bashō

Poem: 行く春や　鳥啼き　魚の目は泪
Romaji: yuku haru ya / tori naki / sakana no me wa namida
My translation:
spring going —
birds cry,
and in the eyes of fish, tears
Notes: Chapter 4: The World of Bashō

Poem: あらたうと　青葉若葉の　日の光
Romaji: ara tōto / aoba wakaba no / hi no hikari
My translation:
how holy —
the light of the sun
on green leaves, young leaves
Kigo: 青葉若葉 aoba wakaba (green leaves; fresh young leaves)
Notes: Chapter 4: The World of Bashō

Poem: 夏草や　兵共が　夢の跡
Romaji: natsukusa ya / tsuwamono-domo ga / yume no ato
My translation:
summer grasses —
all that remains
of warriors' dreams
Notes: Chapter 4: The World of Bashō

Poem: さみだれを　あつめて早し　最上川
Romaji: samidare wo / atsumete hayashi / Mogamigawa
My translation:
gathering all
the rains of May —
swift, the Mogami
Kigo: 五月雨 samidare (May rains; summer rains)
Notes: Chapter 4: The World of Bashō

Poem: 荒海や　佐渡によこたふ　天の河
Romaji: araumi ya / Sado ni yokotau / amanogawa
My translation:
the rough sea —
stretching toward Sado island,
the Milky Way
Notes: Chapter 4: The World of Bashō

Poem: 一家に　遊女も寝たり　萩と月
Romaji: hitotsu ya ni / yūjo mo netari / hagi to tsuki
My translation:
under one roof —
courtesans asleep too,
bush clover and moon
Notes: Chapter 4: The World of Bashō

Poem: 初しぐれ　猿も小蓑を　ほしげなり
Romaji: hatsushigure / saru mo komino wo / hoshige nari
My translation:
the first winter rain —
the monkey too seems to want
a little raincoat
Notes: Chapter 4: The World of Bashō

Poem: うき我を　さびしがらせよ　閑古鳥
Romaji: uki ware wo / sabishigarase yo / kankodori
My translation:
make me lonelier still,
o cuckoo,
wretched as i am
Notes: Chapter 4: The World of Bashō

Poem: 病雁の　夜寒に落ちて　旅寝かな
Romaji: yamigarasu / yosamu ni ochite / tabine kana
My translation:
a sick wild goose
falling in the cold night —
sleeping on the road
Notes: Chapter 4: The World of Bashō

Poem: 行春を　近江の人と　惜しみける
Romaji: yuku haru wo / Ōmi no hito to / oshimi keru
My translation:
lamenting spring's passing
with the people of Ōmi —
how we mourned it
Notes: Chapter 4: The World of Bashō

Poem: 草臥て　宿かるころや　藤の花
Romaji: kutabirete / yado karu koro ya / fuji no hana
My translation:
weary, the hour
to find lodging —
wisteria in bloom
Notes: Chapter 4: The World of Bashō

Poem: 梅が香に　のつと日の出る　山路かな
Romaji: ume ga ka ni / notto hi no deru / yamaji kana
My translation:
into the plum's fragrance —
the sun rising suddenly:
a mountain road
Notes: Chapter 4: The World of Bashō

Poem: 傘に　押しわけみたる　柳かな
Romaji: kasa ni / oshiwakemitaru / yanagi kana
My translation:
pushing aside with my umbrella —
the willow
Notes: Chapter 4: The World of Bashō

Poem: 春雨や　蜂の巣つたふ　屋根の漏り
Romaji: harusame ya / hachi no su tsutau / yane no mori
My translation:
spring rain —
running down the wasp's nest,
the leaking roof
Notes: Chapter 4: The World of Bashō

Poem: うぐひすや　竹の子藪に　老を鳴く
Romaji: uguisu ya / takenoko yabu ni / oi wo naku
My translation:
the warbler —
in the young-bamboo thicket,
singing of old age
Kigo: 鶯 uguisu (warbler; bush warbler); 竹の子 takenoko (bamboo shoots)
Notes: Chapter 4: The World of Bashō

Poem: 寒菊や　粉糠のかかる　臼の端
Romaji: kangiku ya / konuka no kakaru / usu no hata
My translation:
winter chrysanthemum —
rice bran dusted
on the edge of the mortar
Notes: Chapter 4: The World of Bashō

Poem: 月花ヲ医ス　閑素幽栖の　野巫の子有り
Romaji: tsuki hana wo / isu kansoyūsei no / yabu no ko ari
My translation:
curing moon and blossom —
child of the simple hermitage,
a village quack
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: 闇の夜は　吉原ばかり　月夜かな
Romaji: yami no yo wa / Yoshiwara bakari / tsukiyo kana
My translation:
on a dark night —
only Yoshiwara
is moonlit
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: 日の春を　さすがに鶴の　歩みかな
Romaji: hi no haru wo / sasuga ni tsuru no / ayumi kana
My translation:
the first day of spring —
and sure enough, the crane
walks as a crane should
Kigo: 日の春 hi no haru (New Year's spring sunrise)
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: 鐘ひとつ　売れぬ日はなし　江戸の春
Romaji: kane hitotsu / urenu hi wa nashi / Edo no haru
My translation:
not a day without a bell sold —
Edo in spring
Kigo: 江戸の春 Edo no haru (Edo in spring; New Year)
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: 霜の朝や　つつむ生姜　味噌嘗（なめ）
Romaji: shimo no asa ya / tsutsumu shōga / miso name
My translation:
a frosty morning —
ginger wrapped in something,
licking the miso
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: 梅一輪　一輪ほどの　暖かさ
Romaji: ume ichirin / ichirin hodo no / atatakasa
My translation:
one plum blossom —
warmth enough
for one plum blossom
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: 蒲団着て　寝たる姿や　東山
Romaji: futon kite / netaru sugata ya / Higashiyama
My translation:
wrapped in a futon,
the shape of something sleeping —
the Eastern Hills
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: 木枯の地にも落とさぬ　しぐれかな
Romaji: kogarashi no / chi ni mo otosanu / shigure kana
My translation:
the winter gale
doesn't let it reach the ground —
the drizzle
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: おうおうと　いへどもうごかぬ　雪の門
Romaji: ōō to / iedomo ugokanu / yuki no kado
My translation:
hey! hey! i call —
but it doesn't move:
the snowy gate
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: 木枕の　垢や伊吹に　残る雪
Romaji: kimakura no / aka ya Ibuki ni / nokoru yuki
My translation:
grime on the wooden pillow —
and on Mt. Ibuki,
lingering snow
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: 鷹の目の　枯野に居て　吹くあらしかな
Romaji: taka no me no / kareno ni ite / fuku arashi kana
My translation:
with the eye of a hawk,
dwelling in the withered fields —
a storm blowing
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: 時鳥　啼くや湖水の　さざ波かな
Romaji: hototogisu / naku ya kosui no / sazanami kana
My translation:
the cuckoo cries —
on the lake,
small waves
Kigo: 時鳥 hototogisu (little cuckoo; lesser cuckoo)
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: いへどもうごかぬ　雪の門
Romaji: iedomo ugokanu / yuki no kado
My translation:
though i call and call —
the snowy gate won't move
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: 誰か待つ　蝿は来りて　夏になって
Romaji: dare ka matsu / hae wa kitarite / natsu ni natte
My translation:
waiting for someone —
the flies have come around,
summer has arrived
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: 馬の頬　押しけつむや　春の童草
Romaji: uma no hō / oshi ketsumu ya / haru no warabe gusa
My translation:
pressing the horse's cheek —
spring children's grass
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: 花の中に　城ありさくら　郡山
Romaji: hana no naka ni / shiro ari sakura / Kōriyama
My translation:
within the blossoms —
a castle, cherry blossoms:
Kōriyama
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: 苗代の　水にちりうく　花の中
Romaji: nawashiro no / mizu ni chiri uku / hana no naka
My translation:
in the seedbed water,
petals drifting and floating —
within the blossoms
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: 俳論よりも軍書にかなし　芳野山
Romaji: hairon yori mo / gunsho ni kanashi / Yoshinoyama
My translation:
more than a treatise on haiku —
it is a war chronicle,
Mt. Yoshino
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: 卯の花に　さくら合はせる　明け方かな
Romaji: u no hana ni / sakura awaseru / akegata kana
My translation:
deutzia blossoms
meeting the cherry blossoms —
at dawn
Kigo: 卯の花 u no hana (deutzia blossoms)
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: 長松が　寝て居る白は　夏座敷かな
Romaji: Chōmatsu ga / nete iru shiro wa / natsu zashiki kana
My translation:
the white of Chōmatsu
lying down —
a summer parlour
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: 行く雲を　寝て見る隣の　名で御慶
Romaji: yuku kumo wo / nete miru tonari no / na de gyokei
My translation:
watching clouds drift by
while lying down — greeting the new year
under a neighbour's name
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: うめの花　赤いは赤い　はな
Romaji: ume no hana / akai wa akai / hana
My translation:
the plum blossoms —
red ones are red,
blossoms
Kigo: 梅の花 ume no hana (plum blossoms)
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: 水鳥や　むかふの岸へ　つういつうい
Romaji: mizudori ya / mukō no kishi e / tsūi tsūi
My translation:
waterfowl —
toward the far shore,
gliding, gliding
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: 灰捨てて　白梅うるむ　垣根かな
Romaji: hai sutete / shirome urumu / kakine kana
My translation:
dumping the ash —
the white plum blossoms blur,
along the fence
Kigo: 白梅 shirome / shiroume (white plum blossoms)
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: 呼びかへす　鮒売見えぬ　雪の原
Romaji: yobikaesu / funaurisemu / yuki no hara
My translation:
calling back —
the carp-seller out of sight:
a field of snow
Notes: Chapter 5: The Four Sages and Six Masters of the Bashō School

Poem: 昼顔の　砂踏み崩す　暑さかな
Romaji: hirugao no / suna fumikuzusu / atsusa kana
My translation:
the morning glory —
crumbling the sand underfoot,
this heat
Kigo: 暑さ atsusa (heat; the summer heat)
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: 駒の尾に　まだ霧原の　大風引き
Romaji: koma no o ni / mada kirihara no / ōkaze hiki
My translation:
at the horse's tail —
still trailing the great wind
of the misty plain
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: 参銭の　音まれまれに　落葉かな
Romaji: sanzen no / oto mare mare ni / ochiba kana
My translation:
the sound of offerings —
so rare, so rare,
falling leaves
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: 鶯の　いくつも捨てて　初音かな
Romaji: uguisu no / ikutsu mo sutete / hatsune kana
My translation:
the warbler —
discarding so many drafts,
its first song
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: 凩の　一日吹いて　居りにけり
Romaji: kogarashi no / ichinichi fuite / ori ni keri
My translation:
the winter gale —
blowing all day long,
has settled in
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: 山々や　応じこぶしづ　老の春
Romaji: yamayama ya / ōji kobushizu / oi no haru
My translation:
mountain after mountain —
responding, the magnolias:
spring of old age
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: かたびらに　越の日数や　後の月
Romaji: katabira ni / Koshi no nissū ya / nochi no tsuki
My translation:
in a summer robe —
the days counted in Koshi:
the late moon
Kigo: 後の月 nochi no tsuki (late moon; second harvest moon)
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: 花さかぬ　身をすほめたる　柳かな
Romaji: hana sakanu / mi wo subometaru / yanagi kana
My translation:
bearing no blossoms,
contracting its body —
the willow
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: 紫陽花に　おもたき朝日　夕日かな
Romaji: ajisai ni / omotaki asahi / yūhi kana
My translation:
on the hydrangeas —
the heavy morning sun,
the evening sun
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: 足高に　橘は残りて　枯野かな
Romaji: ashitaka ni / tachibana wa nokori te / kareno kana
My translation:
standing tall —
the mandarin orange remains:
a withered field
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: 朝顔に　釣瓶とられて　もらひ水
Romaji: asagao ni / tsurube torarete / morai mizu
My translation:
the morning glory
has captured the bucket —
i'll beg water elsewhere
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: 稲妻の　尾や其のまゝに　かきつばた
Romaji: inazuma no / o ya sono mama ni / kakitsubata
My translation:
the lightning's tail —
just as it is,
an iris
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: 夕顔や　女子の肌の　見ゆる時
Romaji: yūgao ya / joshi no hada no / miyuru toki
My translation:
the evening glory —
the moment
a girl's skin shows
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: 落鮎や　日に日に水の　しづまる磯かな
Romaji: ochiayu ya / hi ni hi ni mizu no / shizumaru iso kana
My translation:
the falling ayu —
day by day the water
settling at the shore
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: 蚊をやく　龍眼肉の　閨の私語
Romaji: ka wo yaku / ryūganniku no / neya no sasame goto
My translation:
burning mosquitoes —
longan fruit
whispered talk in the bedchamber
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: 折って後　貴ふ声あり　垣の梅
Romaji: otte nochi / tōto koe ari / kaki no ume
My translation:
after breaking it —
a voice calling precious!"
plum at the fence
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: 蚊の声の　しらむに寂し　軒の雨
Romaji: ka no koe no / shiramu ni samishi / noki no ame
My translation:
the mosquito's voice
fading into light —
rain at the eaves
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: 低きかたへ　水のあはづや　初あらし
Romaji: hikuki kata e / mizu no awazu ya / hatsu arashi
My translation:
toward the low place —
the water not yet meeting:
first autumn storm
Kigo: 初嵐 hatsu arashi (first autumn storm)
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: 梅咲いて　朝寝の家と　成りにけり
Romaji: ume saite / asane no ie to / nari ni keri
My translation:
the plum has bloomed —
it has become
a house of morning sleep
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: 梅が香や　南吹く夜の　肱枕
Romaji: ume ga ka ya / minami fuku yo no / hiji makura
My translation:
the plum's fragrance —
a night of south wind,
elbow as pillow
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: 川上の　虹を白に眺む　夜あけかな
Romaji: kawakami no / niji wo shiro ni nagamu / yoake kana
My translation:
upstream —
watching the rainbow turn white:
the break of day
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: 梅もどき　としの尾や都の　孤釣り
Romaji: umemOdoki / toshi no o ya miyako no / ko-tsuri
My translation:
fake plum —
the year's end in the capital,
a lone fisherman
Kigo: 年の尾 toshi no o (year's end)
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: 紅梅に　青く横たふ　寛かな
Romaji: kōbai ni / aoku yokotau / hiro kana
My translation:
against the red plum —
lying green across it,
the calm
Notes: Chapter 6: The Course of the Bashō Style

Poem: あらし吹く　草の中より　瓜のほひかな
Romaji: arashi fuku / kusa no naka yori / uri no nioi kana
Notes: Chapter 7: The Stirring of the Mid-Edo Revival

Poem: 名月や　沖の高みな　ひかりもあり
Romaji: meigetsu ya / oki no takami na / hikari mo ari
My translation:
the harvest moon —
even the distant offshore heights
have their light
Notes: Chapter 7: The Stirring of the Mid-Edo Revival

Poem: 白菊や　浅黄に見ゆる　折もあり
Romaji: shiragiku ya / asagi ni miyuru / ori mo ari
My translation:
white chrysanthemums —
sometimes they appear pale blue,
in certain light
Notes: Chapter 7: The Stirring of the Mid-Edo Revival

Poem: 椿落て　一音皆　心に対ふ
Romaji: tsubaki ochite / hitoto-ne mina / kokoro ni mukau
My translation:
a camellia drops —
one sound, and all
turns toward the heart
Notes: Chapter 7: The Stirring of the Mid-Edo Revival

Poem: 湖の水　鳴く蛙か　こほす蛙か
Romaji: mizuumi no mizu / naku kawazu ka / kobosu kawazu ka
My translation:
the lake's water —
frogs calling, or
frogs spilling it?
Notes: Chapter 7: The Stirring of the Mid-Edo Revival

Poem: 九月尽　遙かに能登の　岬の海
Romaji: kugatsu jin / haruka ni Noto no / misaki no umi
My translation:
the end of the ninth month —
in the distance, the sea
at the cape of Noto
Kigo: 九月尽 kugatsu jin (end of the ninth month)
Notes: Chapter 7: The Stirring of the Mid-Edo Revival

Poem: はるののゆき扇ではらふ　衣紋かな
Romaji: harunono yuki / ōgi de harau / eimon kana
My translation:
spring-field snow —
brushing it off with a fan:
straightening the robe
Notes: Chapter 7: The Stirring of the Mid-Edo Revival

Poem: 薫の梅が香ふく　板戸ころかな
Romaji: kaoru ume ga ka / fuku itado / koro kana
My translation:
the fragrant plum's scent blowing —
a wooden shutter
rolling
Notes: Chapter 7: The Stirring of the Mid-Edo Revival

Poem: 若菜野や　赤裳引きづる　雪の上
Romaji: wakana no ya / akamo hikizuru / yuki no ue
My translation:
the young-greens field —
a red skirt trailing
across the snow
Kigo: 若菜 wakana (young greens; spring greens)
Notes: Chapter 7: The Stirring of the Mid-Edo Revival

Poem: 蝶飛ぶや　小狐狂ふ　岡のはら
Romaji: chō tobu ya / kogitsune kuruu / oka no hara
My translation:
butterflies flying —
a small fox frolicking
on the hillside plain
Notes: Chapter 7: The Stirring of the Mid-Edo Revival

Poem: 白根牡丹や　只一輪の　盛り草の花
Romaji: shirane botan ya / tada ichirin no / sakari kusa no hana
My translation:
Shirane peony —
just one bloom,
a flower at its peak among the grasses
Notes: Chapter 7: The Stirring of the Mid-Edo Revival

Poem: 夕風や　野川を蝶の　越えしより
Romaji: yūkaze ya / nogawa wo chō no / koeshi yori
My translation:
the evening wind —
since the butterfly crossed
the field stream
Notes: Chapter 7: The Stirring of the Mid-Edo Revival

Poem: 人恋し　灯ともしごろを　さくらちな
Romaji: hito koishi / hi tomoshi goro wo / sakura chi na
My translation:
longing for someone —
at the hour of lighting lamps,
cherry blossoms fall
Notes: Chapter 7: The Stirring of the Mid-Edo Revival

Poem: 行く秋の　草にかくる　流れかな
Romaji: yuku aki no / kusa ni kakuru / nagare kana
My translation:
autumn going —
a stream hidden
in the grasses
Notes: Chapter 7: The Stirring of the Mid-Edo Revival

Poem: 木枯や　市に業の　琴をき
Romaji: kogarashi ya / ichi ni waza no / koto wo ki
My translation:
the winter gale —
at the market, a craftsman's
koto being played
Notes: Chapter 7: The Stirring of the Mid-Edo Revival

Poem: 鶏の鞘に　氷こほる　菜屑かな
Romaji: niwatori no / saya ni kooru / nakuzu kana
My translation:
in the rooster's beak —
ice forming
on the cabbage scraps
Notes: Chapter 7: The Stirring of the Mid-Edo Revival

Poem: 君が代や　二三度し　たると　とし忘れ
Romaji: kimi ga yo ya / ni san do shi / taru to / toshi wasure
My translation:
the age of our lord —
two or three times already
we have forgotten the year
俳人: 蕪村, as Saicho 宰町
Notes: Chapter 8: The Life and Literature of Buson

Poem: 古庭に　鶯略き　ぬ日もすがら
Romaji: furuniwa ni / uguisu naki / nu hi mo sugara
My translation:
in the old garden —
the warbler cries
all through a rainy day
Notes: Chapter 8: The Life and Literature of Buson

Poem: 花守の　身は弓　矢なき　かしかな
Romaji: hanamori no / mi wa yumi / yaki / kashi kana
My translation:
the blossom-guardian's body —
bow without arrow,
oak tree
Notes: Chapter 8: The Life and Literature of Buson

Poem: 夕風や　水青鷺の　脛をうつ
Romaji: yūkaze ya / mizu ao-sagi no / hagi wo utsu
My translation:
the evening breeze —
water striking the legs
of the grey heron
Notes: Chapter 8: The Life and Literature of Buson

Poem: しら梅に　明る夜ばかりと　なりにけり
Romaji: shirame ni / akuru yo bakari to / nari ni keri
My translation:
the white plum —
it has become a night
brightened only by this
Kigo: 白梅 shirome / shiroume (white plum blossoms)
Notes: Chapter 8: The Life and Literature of Buson

Poem: 春雨や　小磯の小貝　ぬるるほど
Romaji: harusame ya / koiso no kogai / nururu hodo
My translation:
spring rain —
enough to wet
the tiny shells on the small shore
Notes: Chapter 8: The Life and Literature of Buson

Poem: 菜の花や　月は東に　日は西に
Romaji: na no hana ya / tsuki wa higashi ni / hi wa nishi ni
My translation:
rapeseed blossoms —
the moon in the east,
the sun in the west
Kigo: 菜の花 na no hana (rapeseed blossoms)
Notes: Chapter 8: The Life and Literature of Buson

Poem: さみだれや　大河を前に　家二軒
Romaji: samidare ya / taiga wo mae ni / ie ni ken
My translation:
the May rains —
facing the great river,
two houses
Kigo: 五月雨 samidare (May rains; summer rains)
Notes: Chapter 8: The Life and Literature of Buson

Poem: 方百里　雨雲よせぬ　ぼたんかな
Romaji: hō hyakuri / amagumo yosenu / botan kana
My translation:
for a hundred leagues around —
no rain cloud approaches:
the peony
Notes: Chapter 8: The Life and Literature of Buson

Poem: 我と来て　遊べや親の　ない雀
Romaji: ware to kite / asobe ya oya no / nai suzume
My translation:
come play with me —
you, sparrow,
with no parent either
Notes: Chapter 10: The Individuality of Issa

Poem: 初夢に　故郷を見て　泪かな
Romaji: hatsuyume ni / furusato wo mite / namida kana
My translation:
in my first dream —
i saw my home village,
and wept
Kigo: 初夢 hatsuyume (first dream of the year)
Notes: Chapter 10: The Individuality of Issa

Poem: 父あり て　明の見たし　草の露
Romaji: chichi arite / asu mo mitashi / kusa no tsuyu
My translation:
my father is here —
i want to see tomorrow too,
the dew on the grass
Kigo: 草の露 kusa no tsuyu (dew on grass)
Notes: Chapter 10: The Individuality of Issa

Poem: 雪の日や　故郷人の　ぶあしらひ
Romaji: yuki no hi ya / furusato bito no / buashirai
My translation:
a snowy day —
the cold reception
of home-village people
Notes: Chapter 10: The Individuality of Issa

Poem: 心からし　なの雪に降られけり
Romaji: kokoro karashi / na no yuki ni / furarekeri
My translation:
from the heart —
fallen upon by the snow
of the plain
Notes: Chapter 10: The Individuality of Issa

Poem: 五十 甥 天窓をかくす　扇かな
Romaji: gojū oi / tenmado kakusu / ōgi kana
My translation:
fifty —
hiding the skylight
with a fan
Notes: Chapter 10: The Individuality of Issa

Poem: 露の世は　露の世ながら　さりながら
Romaji: tsuyu no yo wa / tsuyu no yo nagara / sari nagara
My translation:
this world of dew —
yes, it is only a world of dew,
and yet... and yet...
Notes: Chapter 10: The Individuality of Issa

Poem: 六十　踊る夜もなく　過ごしけり
Romaji: rokujū / odoru yo mo naku / sugoshi keri
My translation:
sixty —
not a single night
of dancing has passed
Notes: Chapter 10: The Individuality of Issa

Poem: 沙汐浜を　反故にして　飛ぶ千鳥かな
Romaji: sachio hama wo / hōgu ni shite / tobu chidori kana
My translation:
leaving the sandy shore
as waste paper —
flying plovers
Notes: Chapter 10: The Individuality of Issa

Poem: 瘦せ蛙　負けるな一茶　是にあり
Romaji: yasegaeru / makeru na Issa / kore ni ari
My translation:
thin frog —
don't give up, Issa
is here
Notes: Chapter 10: The Individuality of Issa

Poem: やれ打つな　蝿が手を摺り　足を擦る
Romaji: yare utsu na / hae ga te wo suri / ashi wo suru
My translation:
don't swat it —
the fly is rubbing
its hands and feet together
Notes: Chapter 10: The Individuality of Issa

Poem: 大仏の柱や　汐干の跡の水
Romaji: daibutsu no / hashira ya shiohiru / ato no mizu
My translation:
the great buddha's pillar —
water left behind
by the ebbing tide
Kigo: 汐干 shiohiru (ebb tide; spring low tide)
Notes: Chapter 11: The Maturation of the Kasei Era

Poem: うすうすと　南天赤し　今朝の雪
Romaji: usuusu to / nanten akashi / kesa no yuki
My translation:
faintly, faintly —
the nandina's red berries
this morning's snow
Notes: Chapter 11: The Maturation of the Kasei Era

Poem: 白ぎくや　籬をめぐる　忘れ水
Romaji: shiragiku ya / magaki wo meguru / wasuremizu
My translation:
white chrysanthemums —
water wandering round
the fence, and forgotten
Notes: Chapter 11: The Maturation of the Kasei Era

Poem: 秋来ぬと　目にはさやかに　見えねども
Romaji: aki kinu to / me ni wa sayaka ni / mienedomo
My translation:
autumn has come —
though not yet clearly seen
by the eye
Kigo: 秋来ぬ aki kinu (autumn has come)
Notes: Chapter 11: The Maturation of the Kasei Era

Poem: うつかりと　名所の中に　田打つ鳥
Romaji: utsukari to / meisho no naka ni / ta utsu tori
My translation:
absentmindedly —
in the middle of a famous place,
a bird tilling the field
Kigo: 田打つ ta utsu (tilling the field; spring plowing)
Notes: Chapter 11: The Maturation of the Kasei Era

Poem: 苗代や　小蛇のわたる　夕の雪
Romaji: nawashiro ya / kojа no wataru / yū no yuki
My translation:
the seedbed —
a small snake crossing
in the evening snow
Notes: Chapter 11: The Maturation of the Kasei Era

Poem: 海にすむ　魚の如　身を月涼し
Romaji: umi ni sumu / sakana no goto / mi wo tsuki suzushi
My translation:
like a fish
living in the sea —
my body, cool in the moonlight
Notes: Chapter 11: The Maturation of the Kasei Era

Poem: 長き夜や　思ひあまりの　泣寝入り
Romaji: nagaki yo ya / omoi amari no / nakineiri
My translation:
the long night —
overwhelmed by feeling,
crying myself to sleep
Notes: Chapter 11: The Maturation of the Kasei Era

Poem: 蝶老てたましひ　菊にあそぶかな
Romaji: chō oite / tamashii kiku ni / asobu kana
My translation:
the butterfly grown old —
its spirit
plays among the chrysanthemums
Notes: Chapter 11: The Maturation of the Kasei Era

Poem: 人恋し　雪の朝気を　ただひとり
Romaji: hito koishi / yuki no asake wo / tada hitori
My translation:
longing for someone —
in the snowy morning light,
utterly alone
Notes: Chapter 11: The Maturation of the Kasei Era

Poem: 山中や　笠に落葉の　音ばかり
Romaji: yamanaka ya / kasa ni ochiba no / oto bakari
My translation:
deep in the mountains —
only the sound of falling leaves
on my hat
Notes: Chapter 11: The Maturation of the Kasei Era

Poem: 山門を出ればゆく物みなあをし
Romaji: sanmon wo / dereba yuku mono / mina aoshi
My translation:
leaving the temple gate —
everything that goes
is green
Notes: Chapter 11: The Maturation of the Kasei Era

Poem: 魚くうて口なまぐさし　昼の月
Romaji: sakana kuute / kuchi namagusashi / hiru no tsuki
My translation:
having eaten fish —
the mouth tastes of the sea:
the moon at noon
Kigo: 昼の月 hiru no tsuki (noon moon)
Notes: Chapter 11: The Maturation of the Kasei Era

Poem: 草山や　潮のびてくる　春の雁
Romaji: kusayama ya / shio nobite kuru / haru no kari
My translation:
grassy mountains —
the tide coming in:
geese of spring
Kigo: 春の雁 haru no kari (spring geese)
Notes: Chapter 11: The Maturation of the Kasei Era

Poem: 魚くうて　口なまぐさし　昼の月
Romaji: sakana kuute / kuchi namagusashi / hiru no tsuki
My translation:
having eaten fish —
the mouth tastes raw,
moon at noon
Kigo: 昼の月 hiru no tsuki (noon moon)
Notes: Chapter 11: The Maturation of the Kasei Era

Poem: 松風や　時うつりして　海苔の寄る
Romaji: matsukaze ya / toki utsuri shite / nori no yoru
My translation:
the pine wind —
time passing,
the seaweed gathering
Notes: Chapter 11: The Maturation of the Kasei Era

Poem: 塩買ひて　かへる径や　落葉時
Romaji: shio kaite / kaeru michi ya / ochiba toki
My translation:
returning home
with salt bought —
the season of falling leaves
Notes: Chapter 11: The Maturation of the Kasei Era

Poem: 卯の花の　満ちたり月は　廿日頃
Romaji: unohana no / michitari tsuki wa / hatsuka goro
My translation:
the deutzia in full bloom —
the moon is
around the twentieth
Notes: Chapter 11: The Maturation of the Kasei Era

Poem: 梅散るや　夜の道具市
Romaji: ume chiru ya / yoru no dōgu ichi
My translation:
the plum petals scatter —
the night antiques market
Notes: Chapter 11: The Maturation of the Kasei Era

Poem: 蝉の音に添ふて　家々に結ふ　粽かな
Romaji: semi no ne ni / soute ie-ie ni / musubu chimaki kana
My translation:
to the cicada's cry —
in house after house,
tying the rice dumplings
Kigo: 蝉 semi (cicada); 粽 chimaki (rice dumpling; summer food)
Notes: Chapter 11: The Maturation of the Kasei Era

Poem: 乳を隠す　泥手わりなき　田植かな
Romaji: chichi wo kakusu / dote warinaki / taue kana
My translation:
hiding the breast —
muddy hands, nothing for it,
rice planting
Notes: Chapter 12: The Expansion of the Tenpō Era and the Late Edo Period

Poem: 秋風や　板絵馬さわぐ　蔵の神
Romaji: akikaze ya / itaema sawagu / kura no kami
My translation:
autumn wind —
the wooden votive horse rattling,
the storehouse deity
Notes: Chapter 12: The Expansion of the Tenpō Era and the Late Edo Period

Poem: ふゆの夜や　針うしなうて　おそろしき
Romaji: fuyu no yo ya / hari ushinaute / osoroshiki
My translation:
a winter night —
having lost the needle,
a terrifying thing
Kigo: 冬の夜 fuyu no yo (winter night)
Notes: Chapter 12: The Expansion of the Tenpō Era and the Late Edo Period

Poem: 春の雪ゆきの遠山　見えて降る
Romaji: haru no yuki / yuki no tōyama / miete furu
My translation:
spring snow —
the far mountains visible
as it falls
Kigo: 春の雪 haru no yuki (spring snow)
Notes: Chapter 12: The Expansion of the Tenpō Era and the Late Edo Period

Poem: 五月雨や　猫かりに来る　船の者
Romaji: samidare ya / neko kari ni kuru / fune no mono
My translation:
the May rains —
a sailor coming
to borrow the cat
Kigo: 五月雨 samidare (May rains; summer rains)
Notes: Chapter 12: The Expansion of the Tenpō Era and the Late Edo Period

Poem: 山風に　星のつぶだつ　さむかな
Romaji: yamakaze ni / hoshi no tsubusuku / samu kana
My translation:
in the mountain wind —
the stars sharp and hard,
the cold
Notes: Chapter 12: The Expansion of the Tenpō Era and the Late Edo Period

Poem: 雪解けや　車はさうな　障子かげ
Romaji: yukidoke ya / kuruma wa sō na / shōji kage
My translation:
the thaw —
a cart might pass,
the shoji's shadow
Notes: Chapter 12: The Expansion of the Tenpō Era and the Late Edo Period

Poem: 三日月の　光ばかりの　夕涼み
Romaji: mikazuki no / hikari bakari no / yūsuzumi
My translation:
just the light
of the crescent moon —
evening cool
Notes: Chapter 12: The Expansion of the Tenpō Era and the Late Edo Period

Poem: 月澄む　馬の座敷を　ほのぼのる人の声
Romaji: tsuki sumu / uma no zashiki wo / honobonoru hito no koe
My translation:
the moon clears —
in the horse's parlour,
a voice glowing faintly
Kigo: 月澄む tsuki sumu (moon clearing; clear autumn moon)
Notes: Chapter 12: The Expansion of the Tenpō Era and the Late Edo Period

Poem: 海を見て　戻れば霞む　戸口かな
Romaji: umi wo mite / modoreba kasumu / toguchi kana
My translation:
after seeing the sea —
coming back, the doorway
is hazy
Notes: Chapter 12: The Expansion of the Tenpō Era and the Late Edo Period

Poem: 石坂の　照りつけられて　蝉の声
Romaji: ishizaka no / teritsuke rarete / semi no koe
My translation:
the stone slope
beating down heat —
the cicada's cry
Notes: Chapter 12: The Expansion of the Tenpō Era and the Late Edo Period

Poem: 菜の花に　入らんとするや　走り波
Romaji: na no hana ni / iranto suru ya / hashiri nami
My translation:
about to enter
the rapeseed blossoms —
a running wave
Kigo: 菜の花 na no hana (rapeseed blossoms)
Notes: Chapter 12: The Expansion of the Tenpō Era and the Late Edo Period

Poem: 鴨の毛の　流れとまるや　芹の中
Romaji: kamo no ke no / nagare tomaru ya / seri no naka
My translation:
the feather of a duck —
coming to rest
among the water-parsley
Notes: Chapter 12: The Expansion of the Tenpō Era and the Late Edo Period

Poem: 冬枯や　沼をたっきの　家二軒
Romaji: fuyugare ya / numa wo tatsu ki no / ie ni ken
My translation:
winter desolation —
over the marsh, two houses
with trees standing
Notes: Chapter 12: The Expansion of the Tenpō Era and the Late Edo Period
